newsitem.title: FRANCE: Reuters French Advertising & Media Digest -June 25.
newsitem.headline: Reuters French Advertising & Media Digest -June 25.

text.p: REUTERS FRENCH ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST
News from Reuters and the French press on Advertising,
Marketing, Media, the Internet and Brand-name Products.
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:
CANNES - Britain's Leo Burnett wins the grand prix for poster
advertising at the International Advertising Festival in Cannes
and British agencies get 48 "Lion" trophies, including 22 gold
Lions. French agencies win only two, a silver Lion for Euro RSCG
BETC for its Evian mineral water campaign, and TBWA for its
Absolut Vodka campaign. (Le Figaro)
CANNES - Three Scandinavian advertising agencies owned by
Interpublic's McCann-Erickson say they formed a joint venture to
focus on the pan-European advertising market. (Reuter)
CANNES - Advertising agency Foote Cone & Belding is in a
stronger position to win global accounts since its parent
company, True North Communications, ended its alliance with
France's Publicis earlier this year, an FCB executive says.
(Reuter)
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:
PARIS - Veteran French oceanographer Jacques-Yves Cousteau, who
popularised underwater exploration with prize-wiunning films,
has died aged 87, his foundation says. (Reuter)
LE MANS - French telephone operator France Telecom is working on
a simplified terminal for Internet access with several European
and North American firms, says Michel Bon, France Telecom's
chairman. (Reuter)
LE MANS - Wanadoo, France Telecom's Internet service provider,
plans a major promotion for this autumn to boost its market
share. The service now has 43,000 subscribers. (Reuter)
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:
PARIS - France's LVMH, stung by a renewed merger pledge between
British drinks groups Guinness and Grand Metropolitan, confirms
it nudges up its stake in Grand Met to 6.3 percent. (Reuter)
PARIS - PSA Peugeot Citroen chairman Jacques Calvet revises down
his market forecast, telling the French carmaker's annual
general meeting he expects French car sales to fall 15.6 percent
in 1997 from a year earlier to 1.80 million registrations.
(Reuter)
PARIS - The management of Cap Gemini, a French computer systems
house, is unhappy over Debis and wants the German group to leave
its capital, business daily La Tribune says. (Reuter)
Paris Editorial, Sue Landau
